historical_timeline.summary: Father died after a two-week illness.
Voted in the presidential election and was arrested.

claims.statement: Susan B. Anthony was born on February 15, 1820, in Adams, Massachusetts, the second child of Daniel and Lucy Read Anthony.
Anthony voted in the 1872 presidential election, was arrested at her Rochester home, and was convicted at Canandaigua, New York; she refused to pay the $100 fine.

Her father, Daniel Anthony, who had not had a day's illness in forty years, was suddenly stricken in November 1862 with what was called acute neuralgia of the stomach and died two weeks later, on November 25, 1862, at 69.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Contemporary description from the authorized biography; the modern cause cannot be determined.

source_links.locator: Chapter on 1897: father died at sixty-nine

claims.statement: Her 1898 biography describes a long-lived family: her mother died at eighty-six, her paternal grandfather lived past ninety-seven, and both maternal grandparents died in their eighty-fourth year.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Causes of death are not recorded in the source.

claims.statement: In January 1891, after weeks of what seemed a persistent la grippe, Anthony collapsed at the Garrison home in Brookline, Massachusetts; pneumonia threatened and she kept to her room for a week.

On July 26, 1895, near the end of an address at Lakeside, Ohio, Anthony stopped abruptly and fainted; from July 30 she spent a month in bed with what was called nervous prostration, described as her first serious illness in seventy-five years.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The contemporary label does not establish a modern cause; no cardiac evaluation is recorded.

claims.statement: Her biographer described her daily habits in the late 1890s: a cold sponge bath each morning, simple food, tea and coffee in moderation, a rest after meals and an hour's rest each afternoon, and fresh air and exercise every day, walking from the station after a day on the train.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Documents her baseline activity and habits; used for the synthetic social history.

claims.statement: In February 1906, although in failing health, Anthony traveled to Washington, D.C.; after returning to Rochester she went to bed, attended by Dr. Ricker and two nurses, and died about three weeks later.
Anthony died at her home on Madison Street in Rochester, New York, at 12:40 a.m. on March 13, 1906, aged 86; the National Park Service records the cause as heart failure and pneumonia.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The documented anchor for the synthetic heart failure episode. Record the death as a fact without graphic detail.
